title: Manual results ingestion input -- one file, a list of independently corroborated final scores
description: Consumed only by pcbf_calculator.orchestration.manual_results_settlement (ingest-manual-results). Every result must carry one or more independent sources; see that module's own docstring 'The corroboration gate' for the acceptance rule (one authoritative source, or two agreeing sources with distinct source_name) -- this schema only enforces SHAPE, never corroboration/business rules, which are checked in code against the parsed structure. competition_raw/home_team_raw/away_team_raw are the bare display names this codebase's own identity resolution already expects (e.g. 'Serie A', 'Bayern Munich') -- never a bookmaker- or results-page-specific format.

scheduled_date.description: UTC calendar date, matching this codebase's own scheduled_date convention everywhere else -- never a bookmaker-local date.

completion_status.description: Only COMPLETED is ever scored -- see REASON_NOT_COMPLETED. The other three values exist so a caller can positively record why a fixture was NOT scored, rather than omitting it silently.

source_name.description: A human-readable identifier for this source (e.g. the site or feed name) -- two sources with the SAME source_name never count as independent corroboration.

evidence_mode.description: ARCHIVED: evidence_hash is a real SHA-256 of independently-archived bytes; operator_attestation must be absent. OPERATOR_ATTESTED: evidence_hash is null; operator_attestation is required and records who explicitly accepted this source in place of an archived hash, and why. This schema only enforces SHAPE -- the consistency between evidence_mode and evidence_hash/operator_attestation, and whether an OPERATOR_ATTESTED source is actually accepted by the command invocation, are checked in code (manual_results_settlement.py's own docstring section 'Operator-attested evidence').

evidence_hash.description: This field's meaning never changes: a cryptographic SHA-256 of independently-archived bytes, or nothing at all. Required (a real hash) when evidence_mode is ARCHIVED. Always null when evidence_mode is OPERATOR_ATTESTED -- never a sentinel string, never a placeholder that looks hash-shaped but isn't.

operator_attestation.description: Present if and only if evidence_mode is OPERATOR_ATTESTED. Records who explicitly accepted this source without an archived hash, when, why, and ties that acceptance to a specific, checksummed source artifact -- never inferred from the file's own say-so alone; ingest-manual-results additionally requires the command invocation itself to explicitly accept the exact source_artifact_sha256 named here (--accept-operator-attested-evidence-for) before any such source counts toward corroboration.

accepted_by.description: Human-readable identity of whoever accepted this source (an operator name/handle) -- never a bare boolean or 'system'.

reason_code.description: Why an archived hash isn't available, e.g. ARCHIVE_UNVERIFIABLE_EGRESS -- a short, typed code, not free text.

source_artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 (bare hex, no 'sha256:' prefix -- this identifies the WHOLE upstream evidence-collection file this source's claim came from, distinct from evidence_hash's own meaning) of the specific file this source's evidence_summary/claim was read from, computed by the tool that produced this row -- never asserted by the file itself without that computation.

source_urls_preserved.description: True iff this source's own source_url is preserved verbatim from the original evidence-collection artifact, so a future successful archive attempt can still target the exact same URL.

authoritative.description: A human judgment call: is this ONE source alone trustworthy enough to accept without a second corroborating source (e.g. the competition's own official site)? See the module docstring's corroboration rule. Independent of evidence_mode -- an OPERATOR_ATTESTED source can still be marked authoritative if the underlying source itself would qualify.
